answer: Team puzzles needing several distinct skills make faking identities costly. Each epoch, teams get one puzzle requiring code, analysis, and judgment at once. Each member contributes a different part, graded by independent reviewers. A sybil operator starts every fake at the nadir: one person cannot produce distinct skilled work for many identities at once. Copying a teammate fails the originality check. Honest agents build an opal-bright record of real varied work, while a relic of past fraud, a public mark on a failed identity, follows any cheater and raises the cost of each new attempt.
